clue.text: See 10
Film enemy keeping old gun elevated

indicators.note: one thing keeping another holds it within, so the enemy word goes around the rest

parts.note: an enemy is a foe

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A film about an enemy holding an antique firearm up high.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is recorded film material, so it stands for film as a noun.

clue.text: No turning back: determined to make start

indicators.note: turning a word back means reading its letters in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written
set, as in set on something, means determined

explanation.surface: A resolve never to retreat, steeling oneself to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning or start of something, typically something unpleasant.

clue.text: Push your luck — in the fitting-room?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for chancing it to see what you can get away with
second meaning, playful: what a shopper does with clothes in a changing room

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading: in a fitting-room you test a garment on yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for chancing bold behaviour, and literally for testing clothes on.

clue.text: E for expert?

parts.note: the letter E is the head (first letter) of the word egg, and an expert intellectual is called by that same compound word

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two parts: E is the front of 'egg', and the whole word is slang for a brainy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Egghead is informal for an intellectual or academic expert.

clue.text: Fresh approach taken about year books

indicators.note: the reworked letters are taken about, i.e. placed around, the abbreviation for year
a fresh version is a new one, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new way of tackling things, adopted over a year, with books.
explanation.walkthrough: The Apocrypha are the books included in some Bibles but not others.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha is a collection of biblical writings of doubtful authority, i.e. a set of books.

clue.text: Trial, then tucked in with a will

parts.note: a trial is a test
to tuck in is to eat heartily, so tucked in means ate

explanation.surface: An exam, followed by a hearty meal, done with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a will' suggests enthusiasm, but here it is the legal sense of having made a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate is the legal term for someone who died having made a valid will.

clue.text: Bolshevik leader's run media company

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace
Sky is a British broadcasting and media company

explanation.surface: A revolutionary heads up a broadcasting firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was one of the leading figures of the Bolshevik revolution of 1917.

clue.text: Force that pulls in giant boost rocked downhill racer

indicators.note: the force symbol goes in among the rearranged letters
something rocked is shaken about, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
g is the symbol for gravitational acceleration, the pull of gravity

explanation.surface: Gravity drawing a huge thrust shaken up: a description of sledging down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobogganist rides a sled down snowy slopes, a racer heading downhill.

clue.text: Made complaint being finally woken

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of the word being
roused means woken from sleep

explanation.surface: Someone grumbled at being woken up at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To groused is to have grumbled, i.e. complained.

clue.text: Tousled beauty had fun avoiding Romeo

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person

indicators.note: avoiding the letter means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: revelled means made merry, had fun
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An attractive person enjoyed themselves away from their lover, looking rumpled.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishevelled describes untidy, rumpled hair or clothes, just as tousled does.

clue.text: Enjoyably nostalgic experience: eruption of Vesuvius?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that pleasantly recalls earlier times
second meaning, whimsical: Vesuvius's eruption of AD 79 was literally an explosion long ago

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading as playful: the volcano that buried Pompeii gave a blast in ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a song, object or memory that brings back the past with pleasure.

clue.text: Debtor has ground in wetlands area

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken and reformed

explanation.surface: A person in debt has land in a marshy region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Broads are a network of rivers and shallow lakes in Norfolk and Suffolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norfolk Broads are a famous region of waterways and marshes, a wetland area.

clue.text: Girl dancing with men shows mischievous spirit

indicators.note: letters that dance move around, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl dancing with some men is full of impishness.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for unexplained mechanical faults.

clue.text: Something from poissonnier, no Moselle ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A diner at the fishmonger's, skipping the German wine, orders something.
explanation.walkthrough: A poissonnier is a fishmonger or fish cook (French); Moselle is a German wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a flatfish one buys from a fishmonger.

clue.text: Spend penny — allowed to go in river?

indicators.note: these letters are allowed to go in, i.e. inserted into, the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Using a toilet ('spend a penny') with permission to relieve oneself in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend a penny' is British slang for using a public toilet, but 'Spend' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to use up or exhaust, i.e. spend resources.

clue.text: Worried singer Jones grabbing weapon

indicators.note: the singer's name grabs, i.e. holds within it, the weapon

parts.note: Aled Jones is a Welsh singer and broadcaster
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A Welsh singer anxiously snatches up a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed means frightened or anxious, i.e. worried.

clue.text: Democrat in a garment gives speech

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in, i.e. inside, the following words

parts.note: a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: A Democrat in a frock delivering a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech made to an audience.

clue.text: Fibbed about keeping small Post Office sack

indicators.note: the turned word keeps, i.e. holds inside it, the abbreviations
about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: fibbed means lied

explanation.surface: Lied about holding a little mailbag from the Post Office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a mailbag noun but is the verb meaning to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to plunder or pillage a place, as soldiers sack a town.

clue.text: Plain in Peru oddly blowy do they say?

indicators.note: this asks how the words are pronounced, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: the odd letters of Peru (first and third) give PR, and blowy means airy: said together they make PR-AIRY

explanation.surface: Is the plateau in Peru windy, people ask?
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large open grassland, a plain.

clue.text: Flat ground helping American university

parts.note: a plate, as in a plateful, is a helping of food

explanation.surface: Helping an American college with its level land.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an area of high level land, flat ground.

clue.text: Animal beginning to eat: more ginger brought round

indicators.note: the comparative is brought round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: ginger hair is red, so more ginger is redder

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of the word eat

explanation.surface: A creature starts to eat, its coat seeming more ginger as it comes round.
explanation.definitionFit: The red deer is a large deer species of Europe and Asia, an animal.

clue.text: One's seen in Modi's land, an Asian nation

indicators.note: the first word is seen in, i.e. placed inside, the country

parts.note: Narendra Modi is Prime Minister of India
read as the plural word ones

explanation.surface: Someone visiting India, from another Asian nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is an archipelago country of Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Instrument transformed satellite upgrade

indicators.note: transformed letters are changed in form, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A device has improved a satellite after an upgrade.
explanation.definitionFit: The pedal steel guitar is a stringed instrument heard in country music.

clue.text: Suggest one opens the letters

indicators.note: one opens the letters, i.e. gets inside them

parts.note: the post is the mail, the letters delivered
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone proposes opening the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward an idea or suggest it as a basis for argument.

clue.text: R.E.M. in to see musical technique

indicators.note: the band name goes in, i.e. inside, the following little word

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Going to see the band R.E.M. for their musical skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremolo is a wavering effect produced by rapid repetition of a note.

clue.text: Brute leaving Black Death area of London

indicators.note: the letter leaving means it is dropped from the word

parts.note: a brute is a beast
end means death, the end of life

explanation.surface: A savage leaves the Black Death behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Death was the medieval plague; B is the pencil abbreviation for black.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End is the historically working-class district east of the City of London.

clue.text: See 21
